title: Personal/sick leave immediately before or after scheduled vacation - 2015 evidence
summary: A restricted 2015 employee-case memo explicitly states a company policy that personal/sick leave could not be used immediately before or after scheduled vacation to extend the vacation. The employee-specific case details are intentionally excluded.

claims.claim: A November 2015 HR memo explicitly states that company policy prohibited using personal/sick leave before or after a scheduled vacation to extend the vacation, and says the rule applied to all employees.

evidence.note: The source is an employee-specific case memo. Employee identity, case details, and raw text are excluded.

steps: Do not operationally apply this historical rule until current policy authority is confirmed.
decisions: Whether a leave request adjacent to scheduled vacation is governed by a current equivalent rule or an exception.
outputs: Leave approval/denial decision under the governing current policy
controls: A single case memo can evidence that a policy statement existed in 2015 but cannot establish that the rule remains current.
Keep employee-specific leave facts out of generalized knowledge.
unresolved_questions: Does current RTEC policy still prohibit personal/sick leave immediately before or after scheduled vacation, and what exceptions/approval authority apply?
Which handbook/policy source formally established this 2015 rule?
automation_candidates: Leave-request validation could flag adjacency to scheduled vacation for human review only after current policy and exceptions are validated.

provenance.notes: Restricted source; raw content and employee-specific facts are not stored in GitHub.
